title: Copy a switch
summary: A light that is halfway on becomes a bucket that tips about half the time.

cards.text:
Train an ordinary on-or-off unit first.
Then let a bucket’s tipping rate stand in for that brightness.

lines: In 10 moments the bucket should tip about 5 times.

question.prompt: The copied brightness is 0.2. In 10 moments, about how many tips?
question.simpler: Multiply the brightness by the number of moments.

question.prompt: You need many moments before the count is a fair copy.
question.why: A short window is a noisy guess at the rate.
question.simpler: The copy is an average, not the first moment.

recall.question: A unit that is off should make the bucket do what?

deeper.note: Diehl and colleagues scaled weights so the buckets did not tip every single moment and saturate. ReLU, which can be truly off, is the natural source.

paper.title: Fast-classifying, high-accuracy spiking deep networks through weight and threshold balancing
paper.venue: International Joint Conference on Neural Networks
paper.section: The weight and threshold balancing method.

terms.plain: a rate standing in for a ReLU
terms.definition: Turn a trained non-spiking network into a spiking one by matching activations with firing rates.
